title: Design manifest
description: What the prototype tool prints for a design: `aidd prototype --screens` prints its screens, `aidd prototype --components` prints its component contract, and `aidd prototype --shots` prints the fidelity pass's views, each as JSON read from the design, never kept by hand. A person or an agent reads it instead of parsing the design's HTML, and `stories` checks the built UI's stories against the components. A new optional key may be added in a minor release; a renamed or removed key bumps `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape. A new key keeps it; a renamed, removed, or retyped key bumps it. It is the version of this output, and the design names its own format on its `<html>` (`data-aidd-prototype`).

screens.description: `--screens`: the design's screens in the order it draws them.

id.description: The screen's id. In the product prototype it is `<flow>:<screen>`, as a link names it.

title.description: The screen's title, as the design names it.

parent.description: The id of the screen this one returns to, or null when the screen names none.

initial.description: The state the viewer opens first: the one the design declares when the screen has it, else its first state. Null when the screen has no state.

states.description: The screen's states, in the order the screen draws them.

components.description: `--components`: every part the design names, so the built UI's components and stories match it by name. Each list is sorted, so the same design always gives the same output.

name.description: The component's name, lowercase words joined by hyphens.

variants.description: Each variant the design names. A component with none has `default`.

screens.description: The screens that use it. None means the chrome, on every screen.

testids.description: The test ids its parts carry.

shots.description: `--shots`: the views the fidelity pass takes, sized to the change, in the order to take them. The prototyping skill's design review says which change takes which. It never lists none: a component or a screen the design does not have is a problem the command names.

screen.description: The screen's id, as `--screens` gives it.

frame.description: The device frame, by its id in the device table.

text.description: The text size, in percent: 200 checks text resized to 200% (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4).

dir.description: The text direction: `rtl` checks a right-to-left layout.

purpose.description: Why the view is taken. `matrix`: a state of a new or reshaped screen. `text-200` and `rtl`: a screen's fullest state at 200% text or right to left, or the changed component at 200% text. `overview`: a screen a changed component appears on, as a person sees it first. `states`: where the state check reads the component's interaction states, on one variant. `narrow`: the component at the narrowest frame (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10).

variant.description: With `states`: its variant, `default` when it names none.

link.description: The view's deep link in the viewer, at actual size: open the page's address with it.

file.description: The screenshot's name: `<screen>-<state>-<frame>-<theme>`, then `-text-200`, `-rtl`, or `-<component>-<variant>`, then `.png`.
